title: Grateful Dead Live at Polo Field, Golden Gate Park on 1967-01-14
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > CDR > CDR > EAC(secure) > Cool Edit(remove isolated pops) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Historic Human Be‑In show with a smoking Morning Dew and solid Viola Lee Blues, captured on a hiss‑filled but listenable soundboard tape.
ai_review.review: The three‑track set from the Jan 14 1967 Human Be‑In is famous for its early, emotionally charged rendition of “Morning Dew” and a raw, powerful “Viola Lee Blues”.  The recording is a soundboard source that suffers from hiss, occasional muddiness and drop‑outs, yet most listeners find the lo‑fi character adds nostalgic charm.  Jerry’s guitar work and Phil’s bass foundation are repeatedly praised, while the on‑stage flute (Charles Lloyd) and the “Good Morning Little Schoolgirl” are viewed as distractions.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews highlight exceptional musical moments (Morning Dew, Viola Lee) and give high star ratings, while noting consistent but tolerable recording flaws; the weighted average yields a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeable hiss and occasional muddiness/drop‑outs; some call it C+ or “pretty bad”, but most agree the tape is listenable and its lo‑fi texture adds historic atmosphere.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Three songs taken from the Human Be‑In; ordering is sometimes debated but the flow peaks with the heartfelt Dew and the high‑energy Viola Lee, making the short set feel like a historic snapshot.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for tight, emotional guitar work and vocal delivery; one reviewer notes a minor mistake near the end of Dew but overall calls his playing “great” and “acid‑assassin”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as providing a solid bass foundation (“Phil bombs”), occasionally shouting “slow down”; another calls him a “wobbly pillar” in contrast to his usual strength.
band_member_comments.Keys: Flute (likely Charles Lloyd) is called distracting by many, though some reviewers find it an interesting, psychedelic addition.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming receives high praise on Dew and Viola Lee; several reviewers argue Mickey Hart may also be present, noting the dual‑drum feel.
